choosing-your-first-humanoid-robot.alt: Three linked panels connect input object, workflow and finished result, with lighting, surfaces, exceptions and frequency below.
choosing-your-first-humanoid-robot.caption: Write down the task boundary and operating conditions before reviewing robots.

choosing-your-first-humanoid-robot.alt: A three-step staircase rises from documentation through representative trial to configuration review.
choosing-your-first-humanoid-robot.caption: Each step should answer a specific question before the next commitment.

robot-price-vs-total-project-cost.alt: Three equal-width budget bands show acquisition, integration and operation without implying numeric cost proportions.
robot-price-vs-total-project-cost.caption: Keep acquisition, integration and operating scope visible as separate budget lines.

robot-price-vs-total-project-cost.alt: An illustrative quote comparison table distinguishes included, optional and unconfirmed scope for two anonymous offers.
robot-price-vs-total-project-cost.caption: A missing line item is a supplier question, not a zero-cost assumption.

how-to-read-a-humanoid-robot-spec-sheet.alt: Two schematic arms hold identical blocks at different horizontal reaches; no numeric capacity is asserted.
how-to-read-a-humanoid-robot-spec-sheet.caption: Payload figures need posture and measurement conditions to become useful.

how-to-read-a-humanoid-robot-spec-sheet.alt: A central specification node connects to model revision, test workload, measurement method and source date.
how-to-read-a-humanoid-robot-spec-sheet.caption: Preserve the context beside each specification in your comparison sheet.

bipedal-wheeled-or-stationary-humanoid.alt: Three stylized humanoid upper bodies are paired with legs, a wheeled base and a workstation pedestal.
bipedal-wheeled-or-stationary-humanoid.caption: Evaluate mobility as a system choice tied to routes and workstations.

bipedal-wheeled-or-stationary-humanoid.alt: A simple floor plan marks a dashed route between workstation and charging, with a doorway, turning space and floor transition.
bipedal-wheeled-or-stationary-humanoid.caption: Include charging, passage widths and recovery access in the route survey.

development-kit-or-complete-research-pla.alt: Separated actuator-like modules in a kit panel contrast with an assembled schematic robot in a research-platform panel.
development-kit-or-complete-research-pla.caption: Both paths need setup; the learning effort sits in different places.

development-kit-or-complete-research-pla.alt: Four milestone cards progress through assembly, configuration, example execution and a single controlled change.
development-kit-or-complete-research-pla.caption: Plan a first result that demonstrates the complete setup, then preserve it.

choosing-actuators-for-a-robot-project.alt: An actuator shaft is linked to power, control, mechanism and load requirements.
choosing-actuators-for-a-robot-project.caption: Select the actuator with its electrical, software and mechanical dependencies.

choosing-actuators-for-a-robot-project.alt: An unscaled step plot shows conceptual acceleration, holding, rest and movement phases over time.
choosing-actuators-for-a-robot-project.caption: A duty-cycle description reveals demands that a peak value alone cannot describe.

dexterous-hands-versus-simple-grippers.alt: A parallel-jaw gripper around a block is shown beside a stylized hand holding a sphere.
dexterous-hands-versus-simple-grippers.caption: Use the object and required action to decide how much hand complexity is useful.

dexterous-hands-versus-simple-grippers.alt: Four panels illustrate shape, surface texture, starting pose and fragility with distinct test objects.
dexterous-hands-versus-simple-grippers.caption: Include difficult examples and changed starting poses in repeatability trials.

robot-software-access-before-you-buy.alt: Four software and hardware layers descend from task application to SDK, low-level interfaces and exact hardware edition.
robot-software-access-before-you-buy.caption: Ask which layers your purchased edition exposes and under what terms.

robot-software-access-before-you-buy.alt: A baseline-change-validation sequence includes a dashed recovery path returning to the saved baseline.
robot-software-access-before-you-buy.caption: Preserve versions, settings and recovery instructions alongside API examples.

simulation-before-physical-testing.alt: Side-by-side schematic robots represent a simulated model and physical system connected by prediction and measurement arrows.
simulation-before-physical-testing.caption: Plan the hardware comparison before treating a simulation result as evidence.

simulation-before-physical-testing.alt: Four unscaled parameter ranges for contact, mass, friction and latency encourage sensitivity testing.
simulation-before-physical-testing.caption: Track estimated model parameters and test plausible variation.

teleoperation-and-autonomy.alt: Five workflow stages show an illustrative mix of human confirmation and automatic execution, explicitly labeled as an example.
teleoperation-and-autonomy.caption: Describe assistance stage by stage instead of assigning a single autonomy label.

teleoperation-and-autonomy.alt: A three-row intervention ledger records work before, during and after a task, including responsibility.
teleoperation-and-autonomy.caption: Include background preparation and recovery when estimating operating effort.

planning-a-humanoid-pilot.alt: A clear pilot boundary encloses one workflow, known objects, location, hours and owner; other sites and fleet rollout sit outside.
planning-a-humanoid-pilot.caption: Write down what the pilot includes and what it cannot yet establish.

planning-a-humanoid-pilot.alt: A review node branches into continue, revise and stop, each with a distinct reason.
planning-a-humanoid-pilot.caption: A useful pilot supports a decision, including a well-evidenced decision to stop.

battery-runtime-and-uptime.alt: An illustrative operating cycle separates work, waiting, charging, inspection and resumed work without numeric duration claims.
battery-runtime-and-uptime.caption: Log unavailable time by cause to identify useful improvements.

battery-runtime-and-uptime.alt: A robot route leads to a labeled charging station with clear return and service access.
battery-runtime-and-uptime.caption: Include charging and service positions when assessing the operating layout.

building-a-useful-robot-shortlist.alt: A three-stage funnel narrows discovered candidates through requirements checks into trade-off comparison.
building-a-useful-robot-shortlist.caption: Apply mandatory requirements before scoring optional features.

building-a-useful-robot-shortlist.alt: A candidate comparison matrix uses confirmed, follow-up and unknown evidence states rather than invented numeric rankings.
building-a-useful-robot-shortlist.caption: Give important unknowns an owner and resolve them before the relevant commitment.

from-demonstration-to-repeatable-robot-t.alt: Six explicitly illustrative attempts include completions, a miss and an assisted outcome rather than only highlights.
from-demonstration-to-repeatable-robot-t.caption: Repeated trials reveal information that a single edited success cannot provide.

from-demonstration-to-repeatable-robot-t.alt: A central visible-action frame is surrounded by before-stage setup and calibration and after-stage reset and recovery.
from-demonstration-to-repeatable-robot-t.caption: Ask who performs the work before and after the filmed action.

what-belongs-in-a-humanoid-marketplace.alt: Three distinct category panels illustrate a robot, a component shaft and separate kit modules.
what-belongs-in-a-humanoid-marketplace.caption: Category clarity helps visitors find a product suited to their purpose.

what-belongs-in-a-humanoid-marketplace.alt: A product listing anatomy panel lists exact configuration, category, commercial status, dated source and compatibility questions leading to a supplier conversation.
what-belongs-in-a-humanoid-marketplace.caption: Discovery becomes useful when visitors can inspect the source and understand the next step.
